title: Checklist: Did you meet your HR KPIs this year?
summary: How do measure the success of your HR strategy each year? Use this checklist to review your HR efforts and find top HR KPI examples.
body_markdown:
HR key performance indicators (KPIs) help organizations measure how effectively their people strategies support business goals. By tracking HR KPIs, leaders can evaluate workforce performance, identify areas for improvement and better understand HR’s impact on organizational success and profitability.


## Table of contents


- How do HR teams measure success at year-end?
- How are HR KPIs best reviewed?
- How to choose the right HR KPIs for your organization
- Key takeaways
- Measuring HR success: Turn insights into actions
- Frequently asked questions about HR KPIs


## How do HR teams measure success at year-end?


As the year draws to a close, it’s the perfect time to pause and assess how your HR KPIs have performed. Reviewing where you stand now provides valuable insights into the impact of your HR practices on your organization’s success. It also sets the stage for planning next year’s priorities, ensuring your focus remains aligned with both your people strategy and broader business goals. By reflecting on what worked and identifying areas for improvement, you can make more informed decisions that drive future success.


Whether you’ve closely monitored your HR scorecard all year or just want to pull some helpful statistics retroactively, conducting a thorough annual review of your HR KPIs is just as important as choosing the right metrics to measure.


## How are HR KPIs best reviewed?


HR KPIs are best reviewed by combining quantitative workforce metrics with qualitative feedback from employees and business leaders. Rather than evaluating numbers in isolation, organizations should examine trends, compare results against goals and assess how HR outcomes support broader business objectives. A structured review process helps identify both successes and opportunities for improvement.


As you review the past year – or, really, at the close of any business milestone or quarter – take a pause, and use this checklist to make sense of what your HR numbers might be showing you. Doing so will help you draw meaningful conclusions that you can use to improve your people strategy and bottom line in the years ahead.


### 1. Run year-end HR KPI reports


To conduct your annual review, you must first pull together all the relevant numbers by running final HR KPI reports. How this looks will depend on how specific you were at the beginning of the year about your goals as an organization and the relevant HR KPIs.


Remember, the KPIs that you include in your year-end review should be directly linked to your company’s overall objectives, goals and strategies, such as:


- [Strengthening diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI)](https://www.insperity.com/blog/increase-workplace-diversity/)
- Improving hiring practices
- Increasing employee satisfaction


Ideally, your annual HR scorecard will show the value that your people management efforts have delivered to your organization throughout the year.


#### **Top HR KPI examples**


If your HR KPIs weren’t clearly defined at the outset of the year, here’s a useful list. You might be able to retroactively pull some data from your software systems that give you a picture of the strategic and financial value your HR team provided this year.


For many organizations, the following HR KPI examples can help provide a meaningful picture of HR’s impact:


**HR KPI** **What it measures**


Turnover rate Employee retention and workforce stability


Average length of tenure Long-term retention trends


Time to fill open positions Recruiting efficiency


Cost per job applicant Recruiting spend effectiveness


Number of qualified candidates Candidate pipeline quality


Cost per hire Overall hiring costs


Quality of hire Success of hiring decisions


Employee productivity Workforce performance


Employee engagement score Employee sentiment and commitment


Not sure which HR KPIs you should prioritize? For a deeper dive into getting your employees ready to execute on your business strategy and goals, read our article on[strategic HR planning](https://www.insperity.com/blog/5-critical-steps-to-future-proofing-your-human-resources-strategy/) .


### 2. Layer in employee feedback


When reviewing your HR KPIs, it’s also smart to consider other sources of information that show how your people practices are influencing your company’s progress.


Did you conduct a corporate culture, employee satisfaction or employee engagement survey this year? Or did you hold any[stay interviews](https://www.insperity.com/blog/stay-interview-questions/) to gather employee opinions?


If so, pull the results back out so you can compare the employee feedback you gathered against your HR KPIs. Do both tell the same story? Or does your employee feedback contradict what the numbers are showing you?


If you’ve been conducting surveys for a number of years, you can even begin benchmarking the results against past results each year.


### 3. Interview your department leaders


Pulling KPIs and[employee survey](https://www.insperity.com/blog/employee-surveys-how-to-get-the-answers-you-need/) results may be the beginning of your year-end review in HR, but looking at the statistical data should by no means be the end of it.


Once you have the reports and results, you can get more out of the information you’ve collected by wrapping it in live conversations with department heads or other key stakeholders around your organization.


Share the data with them and what you think it yields, and then get their input and experience on a more visceral level. For example, when sharing turnover rate, a department head might tell you about concerns they received leading up to somebody leaving, such as an employee who was struggling with the pay they were receiving.


Here are some questions you can use to guide your conversations with other leaders:


- What have you observed this year as a manager?
- What are the challenges in your department?
- Have you had employees raise any issues or concerns?


Leaders outside of your HR department may easily explain pieces of data that are surprising or confusing from your perspective. Their insights can be invaluable to you as you review HR KPIs and make plans for the following year and beyond.


### 4. Assess HR’s impact on business outcomes


Taking into account not only your HR KPIs, but also employee survey results and insights from your company’s department heads, gives you a more holistic view of the many factors that are driving your HR-related business performance.


Your goal should be to synthesize all of this information to get the best picture of how your HR results are impacting organizational goals. Taking time to understand this comprehensive view of your HR effectiveness allows you to evaluate your people strategies more honestly at year-end.


### 5. Use HR KPI insights to plan for the future


The final piece of your review involves asking important questions and evaluating what trends you see emerging from your HR KPIs, combined with the additional information in your review.


Pull your HR team together and explore:


- What seems to be working?
- What is falling short of our expectations?
- Are any of our HR KPIs moving in the wrong direction?
- What was missing this year that should be added to next year’s strategy?
- What actions should we implement in our strategy based on results from this year?


Remember that some HR KPIs run longer than a year, so you might be looking both backward and forward at the end of a single year.


##
How to choose the right HR KPIs for your organization


Choosing the right HR KPIs starts with understanding your organization’s strategic priorities. The most valuable metrics are those that connect HR activities to measurable business outcomes.


**When selecting KPIs:**


- Identify the business goals your workforce must support.
- Consider your industry, workforce size and growth stage.
- Focus on metrics that can influence decision-making.
- Balance leading indicators (future-focused metrics) with lagging indicators (historical results).
- Review KPI relevance annually as business priorities evolve.


For example, a growing organization may prioritize recruiting metrics such as time-to-fill and cost-per-hire, while a mature organization may focus more heavily on retention, engagement and succession planning measures.


## Key takeaways


- Year-end HR KPI reviews should combine workforce metrics, employee feedback and leadership insights.
- Effective KPI reviews focus on business outcomes, not just HR activities.
- Metrics such as turnover, engagement, quality of hire and time-to-fill provide valuable indicators of HR performance.
- Comparing results over time often delivers more value than reviewing a single year’s data.
- Findings from annual KPI reviews should directly inform next year’s HR strategy.


## Measuring HR success: Turn insights into actions


Measuring the success of your HR practices at the end of the year helps you plan for what’s next more strategically. Analyzing the numbers alongside employee and manager feedback can make your raw HR KPIs more relevant.


Organizations of all sizes can grow faster using measurable, strategic HR practices that get employees aligned with business goals. ## Frequently asked questions about HR KPIs


What are the most important HR KPIs to track?


Common HR KPIs include turnover rate, employee engagement score, time to fill open positions, cost per hire, quality of hire and average employee tenure.


How often should HR KPIs be reviewed?


Most organizations review KPIs monthly or quarterly, then conduct a more comprehensive analysis at year-end.


What is the difference between leading and lagging HR indicators?


Leading indicators help predict future outcomes, while lagging indicators measure results that have already occurred.
